seeds.name: Tomato
seeds.description: One of the most rewarding garden plants. Produces abundantly in warm weather.

growing_steps.step: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost. Plant 1/4 inch deep in seed starting mix.
Keep soil moist and warm (65-85°F). Seeds should germinate in 5-10 days.
When seedlings have 2 true leaves, transplant to larger pots. Begin hardening off.
Transplant outdoors after last frost. Bury stem deep — roots will grow from buried stem.
Install cage or stakes. Begin regular watering schedule. Mulch around base.
Prune suckers for indeterminate varieties. Fertilize every 2-3 weeks.
Watch for pests (hornworms, aphids). Remove yellow leaves at bottom.
Harvest when fruits are fully colored and slightly soft to touch. Pick regularly to encourage production.

tips: Bury the stem deep when transplanting — tomatoes grow roots from the stem
Water at the base, not the leaves, to prevent disease
Prune suckers on indeterminate varieties for larger fruit
Companion plant with basil to repel pests

seeds.name: Lettuce
seeds.description: Fast-growing cool-weather crop. Perfect for beginners and container gardening.
seeds.water: 1 inch per week, keep soil consistently moist

growing_steps.step: Sow seeds directly 1/4 inch deep. Can start indoors or outdoors in cool weather.
Seeds germinate quickly (2-10 days). Keep soil moist with gentle watering.
Thin seedlings to proper spacing. Use thinnings in salads!
Begin light fertilizing. Keep soil consistently moist.
For leaf varieties, begin harvesting outer leaves when 4-6 inches tall.
Harvest head varieties when firm. Cut-and-come-again for leaf types.

tips: Succession plant every 2 weeks for continuous harvest
Bolts (goes to seed) in hot weather — provide afternoon shade
Great for container and windowsill growing
Plant in spring and fall for best results

seeds.name: Basil
seeds.description: Aromatic herb that's easy to grow and essential in the kitchen.
seeds.water: 1 inch per week, don't let soil dry out completely

growing_steps.step: Start seeds indoors 6 weeks before last frost. Press seeds lightly into moist soil.
Seeds need light to germinate. Keep warm and moist. Germination in 5-10 days.
Transplant seedlings when they have 2-3 sets of true leaves.
Move outdoors after last frost or keep on sunny windowsill.
Begin harvesting by pinching off top leaves. This encourages bushier growth.
Pinch off flower buds to keep plant producing leaves. Harvest regularly.

tips: Pinch off flower buds to keep the plant producing leaves
Harvest from the top down to encourage bushy growth
Excellent companion plant for tomatoes
Bring indoors before first frost or take cuttings

seeds.name: Bell Pepper
seeds.description: Colorful and nutritious. Needs warmth and patience but very rewarding.
equipment: Seed starting tray with heat mat

growing_steps.step: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost. Use heat mat for best germination.
Germination takes 7-14 days. Keep soil warm and moist.
Transplant to larger pots when seedlings have 2 true leaves.
Harden off and transplant outdoors when nighttime temps stay above 55°F.
Stake plants for support. Mulch to retain moisture and warmth.
Fertilize when first flowers appear. Remove early flowers to strengthen plant.
Harvest when peppers reach full size. Leave on plant longer for color change (green to red/yellow).

tips: Use a heat mat for faster germination
Remove first few flowers to strengthen the plant
Green peppers left on the plant will turn red, yellow, or orange
Very frost-sensitive — wait until soil is warm to transplant

seeds.name: Cucumber
seeds.description: Prolific producers that grow quickly in warm weather.
seeds.water: 1-2 inches per week, consistent moisture critical

growing_steps.step: Direct sow 1 inch deep after last frost, or start indoors 3 weeks before transplanting.
Germination in 3-10 days. Keep soil warm and moist.
Thin to strongest seedlings at proper spacing. Install trellis.
Mulch heavily to retain moisture. Begin regular watering schedule.
Train vines onto trellis. Watch for cucumber beetles.
Flowers appear — ensure pollinators can reach them.
Harvest when 6-8 inches for slicing, 2-4 inches for pickling. Pick daily.

tips: Grow vertically on a trellis to save space and prevent disease
Harvest frequently to keep plants producing
Inconsistent watering causes bitter fruit
Plant dill nearby to attract beneficial insects

seeds.name: Carrot
seeds.description: Sweet root vegetable that tastes much better homegrown than store-bought.
seeds.sun: Full sun to partial shade (4-6 hours)
seeds.water: 1 inch per week, keep top of soil moist during germination
equipment: Deep container (12+ inches) or raised bed

growing_steps.step: Direct sow seeds 1/4 inch deep in loose, rock-free soil. Do NOT transplant.
Keep soil surface moist. Cover with burlap or row cover to retain moisture.
Germination is slow (14-21 days). Be patient and keep watering.
Thin seedlings to 2-3 inches apart. This is critical for proper root development.
Mulch around plants. Water deeply and consistently.
Hill soil around tops to prevent green shoulders.
Harvest when tops are 1/2 to 3/4 inch in diameter. Loosen soil before pulling.

tips: Carrots must be direct sown — they don't transplant well
Rocky or heavy soil causes forked roots
Mix seeds with sand for easier, more even sowing
Frost actually makes carrots sweeter!

seeds.name: Green Bean
seeds.description: Easy and productive. Bush varieties are great for containers.

growing_steps.step: Direct sow 1 inch deep after last frost. Do not start indoors — beans don't transplant well.
Seeds germinate quickly (4-10 days). Keep soil moist but not waterlogged.
For pole varieties, install support and train vines. Mulch around plants.
Flowers appear. Avoid overhead watering to protect blossoms.
Begin harvesting when beans are firm and snap cleanly. Pick every 2-3 days.
Continue picking to keep plants producing. Bush beans may have a second flush.

tips: Don't soak bean seeds before planting — it can crack them
Pick regularly to keep plants producing
Bush varieties are easier; pole varieties produce more over time
Beans fix nitrogen — great for soil improvement

seeds.name: Strawberry
seeds.description: Sweet berries perfect for containers and hanging baskets.

growing_steps.step: Plant transplants (easier than seed) in spring. Set crown at soil level.
Water regularly. Apply straw mulch around plants to keep berries clean.
Pinch off first-year flowers for June-bearing types to strengthen plants. Everbearing can fruit first year.
Runners will appear — pin down to create new plants or trim to focus energy on fruit.
Berries forming. Install bird netting to protect fruit.
Harvest when fully red. Pick every 2-3 days. Morning harvest is sweetest.
After harvest, trim foliage and mulch heavily for winter protection.

tips: Transplants are much easier than growing from seed
Straw mulch keeps berries clean and prevents disease
Everbearing varieties produce all season long
Great for hanging baskets and containers

seeds.name: Spinach
seeds.description: Nutrient-dense cool-weather green. Fast-growing and easy.
seeds.water: 1 inch per week, keep soil evenly moist

growing_steps.step: Direct sow 1/2 inch deep in cool weather (spring or fall). Can start very early.
Seeds germinate in 5-14 days. Keep soil consistently moist.
Thin seedlings to 4-6 inches apart.
Apply thin layer of compost as side dressing.
Begin harvesting outer leaves when they're large enough to eat.
Harvest entire plant before it bolts, or continue picking outer leaves.

tips: Best grown in spring and fall — bolts in hot weather
Soak seeds overnight for faster germination
Extremely cold hardy — can survive light freezes
Succession plant every 2-3 weeks for continuous harvest

seeds.name: Radish
seeds.description: The fastest vegetable to grow. Harvest in as little as 3 weeks!
seeds.sun: Full sun to partial shade (4-6 hours)

growing_steps.step: Direct sow 1/2 inch deep. One of the easiest seeds to plant.
Seeds germinate in 3-7 days — very fast! Thin to 1-2 inches apart.
Keep soil evenly moist. Radishes grow very quickly.
Check size by gently brushing away soil at base. Harvest when 1 inch diameter.
Don't leave in ground too long — they become woody and pithy. Plant more!

tips: Fastest vegetable to grow — great for kids and beginners
Plant every week for continuous harvest
Gets woody if left too long — harvest on time
Great companion plant — marks rows of slow-germinating seeds

seeds.name: Mint
seeds.description: Incredibly easy to grow (almost too easy). Perfect for beginners.
seeds.water: Keep soil moist, tolerates wet conditions

growing_steps.step: Start from cuttings (easiest) or seeds. Plant in a container to prevent spreading.
If from seed, germination takes 10-15 days. Cuttings root in about a week.
Keep soil moist. Mint is very forgiving.
Pinch growing tips to encourage bushy growth.
Begin harvesting leaves as needed. Cut stems just above a leaf pair.
Harvest regularly — mint is vigorous and benefits from frequent cutting.

tips: ALWAYS grow in containers — mint is extremely invasive in garden beds
Easiest herb to grow from cuttings — just put a stem in water
Many varieties: peppermint, spearmint, chocolate mint, apple mint
Comes back year after year (perennial)

seeds.name: Zucchini
seeds.description: Incredibly productive summer squash. One plant can feed a family!

growing_steps.step: Direct sow 1 inch deep after last frost, or start indoors 2-3 weeks before transplanting.
Fast germination (4-7 days). Keep soil warm and moist.
Thin to strongest plant per hill. Mulch heavily around plants.
Large leaves will shade out weeds. Water at base to prevent powdery mildew.
Flowers appear — male flowers first, then female. Hand-pollinate if needed.
Harvest when 6-8 inches long. Check DAILY — they grow very fast!
Continue harvesting every 1-2 days. One plant can produce 6-10 lbs per week.

tips: Harvest small (6-8 inches) for best flavor — giant zucchini are seedy and bland
Check daily once fruiting starts — they grow incredibly fast
Male flowers appear first — don't worry if first flowers don't produce fruit
One plant is usually plenty for a family
